Never write an occasion string or an `IntakeEmailLog` row by hand: the sweep's and the console's "still owed" reads are `IntakeEmails.owing/1` and `scheduled/3`. `queue/4` renders the shared `Dhc.Email.RichText` vocabulary without inline styles, seals the Intake link, and passes the subject override. Queueing never refuses a template that passed the save-time measure: if HTML escaping pushes the filled body over 2,000 characters, each value is shortened until its escaped form fits its placeholder maximum. The 2,000-character measure must keep matching `packages/email-templates/fixtures/intake-email-measure.json`, which the dashboard counter shares. See the Intake Email row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
44: 
45: The Intake Email template editor (ALE-383) saves through `IntakeEmails.update_template/2`, whose refusals are named reasons (`placeholder_not_allowed`, `template_too_long`, `invalid_template`). Its browser counter (`lib/beginners-workshops/intake-emails/measure.ts`) must keep rendering exactly like `Dhc.Email.RichText` without styles: change both together and keep the shared fixture cases passing on both sides. The editor chip is `RichTextEditor`'s `placeholders` prop; never emit `{{name}}` text into a body. See the template editor row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
46: 
47: Intake Reply addresses (ALE-407) are per-email credentials: `INTAKE_REPLY_DOMAIN` is optional, each enabled delivery stores only a token hash and seals the address in the Oban args, and the resolver is `Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.IntakeReplies.resolve/1`. Hard delete and retention purge remove a person's bindings in their boundary transaction. See the Intake Reply row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
48: 
49: Intake Replies are received and forwarded (ALE-409) through `POST /api/webhooks/resend` (Svix-verified by `Dhc.Resend.Webhook`, raw body via `CacheBodyReader`, route `log: false`): the webhook only calls `IntakeReplies.record_received/2` (one `IntakeReply` row unique on the Resend email id, one `Workers.ReplyWorker` job whose only arg is that id), and `IntakeReplies.forward/2` sends the one forward under `intake-reply-forward:<id>` and records it, so a retry never sends twice. The whole feature is parked until the eval has enough labelled replies (`IntakeReplies.enabled?/0`, `config :dhc, Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.IntakeReplies`, off by default, ALE-414): off, no reply address is minted — Intake Emails keep the shared contact Reply-To, so replies still reach the club inbox as ordinary email — and the webhook verifies the signature but answers `handled: false` recording nothing. Minting and receiving move together deliberately, so a reply address can never be live while the endpoint that receives it ignores deliveries; do not split the switch. Resend reads go through `Dhc.Resend.Receiving` (Req, reuses the full-access `RESEND_API_KEY` unless `RESEND_RECEIVING_API_KEY` overrides it; tests `Req.Test.stub(Dhc.Resend, …)` via `Dhc.ResendReceivingStub`); the forward goes through `Dhc.Email.Mailer`. The row stores no body, subject or address. A forward that cannot be sent on the last attempt is the `:system` command `{:alert_reply_waiting, id}` (`Commands.Replies` → `CoordinatorAlerts`); Reply Actions (ALE-411) extend `forward/2`'s outcome, not the webhook.
50: 
51: Invitation pricing tiers use backend-applied Stripe coupon IDs, not customer-facing promotion codes; see the invitation pricing tier note in `docs/agents/notes.md` for coupon configuration and E2E conventions.
52: 
53: Reply text leaves Phoenix only through `Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.IntakeReplies.ReplyText.extract/1` (ALE-408): the person's new words, quoted history and signatures cut, every URL `[link]`, address `[email]` and phone number `[phone]`, at most 2,000 characters. Jev (ALE-410) and the offline eval both call it, so never hand a classifier the raw `text`/`html`; widen quoting rules there, with a synthetic fixture in `reply_text_test.exs` (never a real email).
54: 
55: Reply Actions (ALE-411) are decided only by `IntakeReplies.Decision` inside `IntakeReplies.forward/2`, before the forward is built, and the intent → command table lives only in the pure `IntakeReplies.ReplyActions`. They run through `execute/3` as `{:intake_reply, intake_reply_id}`, which `Commands` authorizes for exactly `@intake_reply_commands` (never `forfeit_carried_fee`; `withdraw` only with `refund: true`) and only for a recorded reply; the history row carries `intake_reply_id` and no Principal. Every intent is off by default in `config :dhc, Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.IntakeReplies.ReplyActions`; with none of the offered intents on, Jev is never called. See the Reply Actions row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
56: 
57: The Intake Reply Jev boundary is `Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.IntakeReplies.Classifier` (ALE-410): generated operations and request/response schemas come from `https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json` via `mix typesafe.gen`; do not hand-edit `lib/dhc/typesafe/generated/`. `Dhc.TypeSafe.Client` owns Req auth, 429/529 retries and closed error mapping. The classifier re-applies `ReplyText.extract/1` before any outbound request, sends only the sanitized words and a plain-language email type, and pins `jev-1.13.0`. A person's name may remain if they write it in the reply; do not add profile name or email metadata to Jev's state, and keep redacting email addresses, links and phone numbers. Configure `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`; run `mix dhc.intake_replies.eval PATH` on hand-labelled exports kept under ignored `apps/phoenix/priv/intake_reply_eval/`. The eval prints aggregates only; it never stores or prints reply text.
58: 
59: Beginners' Workshop Intake payments open embedded Checkout automatically (`initEmbeddedCheckout`, `redirect_on_completion: if_required`), with Phoenix's existing return operation confirming success. The browser submits the payment POST after mount; GET/prefetch never takes a Seat Hold. `checkout_ui_mode` is frozen with the hold: new holds are `embedded`, pre-migration holds stay `hosted` so their idempotent replays remain identical. Resume a recorded embedded session by retrieving its client secret, not creating again or persisting the secret; wallet display requires the frontend domain registered in Stripe.
60: 
61: Target Inventory Item operations live on `/api/inventory/items*` under the one `Inventory` tag since ALE-289 deleted the legacy slice and moved them onto the freed URLs (slice `inventoryItems.*`); those reads are operator-only by design. The member-facing catalog and own-loan operations (`/api/inventory/catalog/items*`, `/api/inventory/loans/mine*`) are a **separate read model**, not a role variant of the operator viewer — member rows cannot express container, notes, or maintenance facts at all. See the Inventory Item and member catalog rows in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md` before editing the API contract.
62: 
63: The generated API client carries a pnpm patch on `@hey-api/openapi-ts` (`patches/`, recorded in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`): ky v2 eagerly consumes error response bodies into `HTTPError.data`, so the unpatched generated client throws `TypeError: body stream already read` and every `error.errors?.detail` UI falls back. The patch reuses the pre-parsed body through the same interceptor pipeline; `pnpm --filter @dhc/api-client api:generate` (and postinstall) regenerate with it applied.
64: 
65: Sentry noise policy lives at `apps/web/src/lib/api-error-reporter.ts`: expected outcomes are matched by operation, status and validated body, with unexpected failures retained. The generated ky client passes the caller's abort signal through interceptor `options.signal`/`options.kyOptions.signal`, not necessarily `request.signal`; keep cancellation detection on those signals. Error pages render only; hooks own framework error capture.
66: 
67: Every availability-changing inventory command — member request/cancel, operator approve/reject/cancel/checkout/return/date edits, move, maintenance open/close, archive, restore — is implemented **once** in `Dhc.Inventory.AvailabilityCommands.execute(actor, command)` (GH-508, ADR 0023): one private `with_locked_item/2` encodes the lock protocol (container chain `FOR SHARE` root-first, then item `FOR UPDATE`, then loans; a restore peeks only to learn which chain to share-lock and retries from a fresh peek if the container moved) and the re-read under the lock, one `persist/1` translates every partial index and principal FK into a domain reason, and the actor (`{:operator, id}` / `{:member, id}`) is authorized before any read. `OperatorItemLifecycle`, `OperatorLoans`, and `MemberLoans` are facades with unchanged signatures; add a new transition as a `run/4` clause in the boundary, never as a new `Repo.transaction` in a facade. `LoanPolicy` (pure predicates) and `LoanProjection` (operator/member views) are shared by the commands and the queue so advisory readiness and authoritative gates cannot diverge. See the availability-command row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
68: 
69: Every transaction that starts, concludes, cancels or refunds a Workshop payment — member/external start and completion (Registration or compensating Refund), member cancellation, requested Refunds, the Refund fan-out of `cancel_workshop`, Refund submission, Stripe `refund.*` events, reconciliation — is implemented **once** in `Dhc.Workshops.PaymentCommands.execute(actor, command)` (ALE-340, ADR 0027): one private `with_locked/2` encodes the lock order Workshop → Payment Attempt → Registration → Refund (skip levels, never lock upward; Refund-started commands peek unlocked, lock what the Refund points to, re-read and retry, and never take the Workshop lock), Stripe is called only between transactions and its result written after an authoritative re-read under that lock (idempotency keys `workshop-payment-attempt:<id>` / `workshop-refund:<id>`, no lease), one transition table writes every Attempt/Refund status (terminal Refunds ignore later events), and `persist/1` translates the unique indexes into `:already_requested`/`:already_registered`. `Dhc.Workshops` keeps the public functions and delegates; the refund workers only turn job args into a command; `Dhc.Workshops.Refund` is a schema only; refund eligibility predicates live in `Dhc.Workshops.RefundPolicy`, shared with the advisory `refund_eligibility/1`. Add a new payment rule as a `run/2` clause in the boundary, never as a new `Repo.transaction` in `workshops.ex`. See the Workshop row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
70: 
71: Loan commands are split domain-seam-first: the boundary writes every transition as durable rows and emits **no notifications**. The HTTP exposure (ALE-298) attaches keyed notifications *after* the command returns via `Dhc.Inventory.notify_loan_transition/2` → `create_keyed/3`. Wiring `Dhc.Notifications.create/2` into a loan transition is the specific mistake that split exists to prevent. See the operator loan and operator-loan-exposure rows in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
72: 
73: Web Push (ALE-299, ADR 0025) is a **best-effort channel after the notification row**, never a second source of truth: `Dhc.Notifications.signal_created/1` broadcasts *and* enqueues one `Dhc.Notifications.Workers.WebPushWorker` job (Oban queue `:notifications`, `max_attempts: 1` on purpose — a job retry would re-push to browsers that already succeeded) per committed row, and neither can reach the creator. Subscriptions live in `Dhc.Notifications.WebPush` **per browser installation** (endpoint-unique upsert; 404/410 deletes the row) and the API discloses only the VAPID public key, `{id, createdAt}`, and `{removed}`. `web_push_ex` builds the RFC 8291/8292 request and Req sends it (`WebPush.Sender` behaviour, substitute with `:web_push_sender`). VAPID is optional and all-or-nothing via `WEB_PUSH_VAPID_{PUBLIC_KEY,PRIVATE_KEY,SUBJECT}` (generate with `mix web_push_ex.vapid`; unset = `enabled: false`, no jobs); tests use the fixed pair in `config/test.exs`. On the web side `apps/web/src/lib/notifications/web-push/` is pure and `PushManager.subscribe` — the only prompting call — runs only from the toggle click; Playwright's Chromium reports notification permission as denied unless a test grants it, so E2E only sees the "blocked" explanation. The `notifications:self` channel alias must subscribe to the principal's canonical PubSub topic or open dashboards receive nothing. See the Web Push row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
74: 
75: Notifications that can be retried must go through the keyed seam `Dhc.Notifications.create_keyed/3` (ALE-287), not `create/2`, which stays at-least-once for existing unkeyed callers. `create_keyed/3` refuses an open transaction because it signals after its own commit; a caller that already holds locks uses `create_keyed_in_transaction/3` and calls `signal_created/1` only after the outer transaction returns `{:ok, _}`. The key names the logical event; uniqueness is `(principal_id, notification_key)`, so one event notifies many recipients from one key. `Dhc.Notifications.Retention` deletes every Notification older than three months nightly, so a key deduplicates retries only, never long-term "already told" state; keep that in a domain ledger (as loan reminders do). Loan reminders (`Dhc.Inventory.LoanReminders`) treat the durable ledger **as** the schedule rather than scheduling a job per reminder: one pass computes at most one owed occurrence per loan, so delivery and reconciliation are the same code path and a missed tick self-heals. `due_on_revision` is derived from the loan's due date, which is why a due-date edit reschedules reminders without any write on the transition path — the reason loan commands stay reminder-free. Inventory-operator eligibility (active profile + the `inventory.manage` capability) lives in `Dhc.Auth.Capabilities` (`principal_ids_with/2` and `authorize/3`); `RequireSession` and loan notifications both call it, so a leftover role row on an inactive principal cannot hear about loans the plug would 401. See the keyed-notification and loan-reminder rows in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
76: 
77: The operator loan queue (`Dhc.Inventory.OperatorLoanQueue`, ALE-297) is a lock-free, actor-free **read model** over those rows: bucket counts are `length(rows)` of the bucket beside them rather than a second aggregate query, so the queue is deliberately unpaginated. It projects loans through `LoanProjection.operator_view/2` (the successor of `OperatorLoans.operator_view/2`) instead of rebuilding the shape, which is the rule to preserve when adding a bucket or field — a queue row and the operator detail read must not be able to disagree. See the operator loan queue row in `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`.
78: 
79: `mix gen.controllers` scaffolds one controller + JSON renderer + contract test per **slice** — the `operationId` prefix — not per tag, so a domain keeps one tag and one URL root while being served by several controllers (the `Inventory` tag owns `inventoryStructure` and `inventoryItems`). Every operation needs an `operationId` of `<slice>.<action>` whose prefix underscores to the controller filename, and `mise run api-gen` must stay idempotent (only `skip` lines, no new files). See ADR 0003 and the `mix gen.controllers` gotchas in `docs/agents/notes.md`.

1: # E2E TESTING
2: 
3: Playwright end-to-end tests backed by Phoenix and a disposable PostgreSQL database.
4: 
5: ## Running
6: 
7: ```bash
8: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... mise run test-e2e
9: # or
10: pnpm --filter @dhc/web test:e2e
11: ```
12: 
13: Playwright owns the full run lifecycle. Do not manually start PostgreSQL, Phoenix, Supabase, or SvelteKit first.
14: 
15: Run focused specs through the documented mise task (`mise run test-e2e --
16: e2e/example.spec.ts`), not a direct filtered workspace invocation, so the same
17: task environment and server lifecycle are used as full runs.
18: 
19: The suite uses the real Stripe test API and rejects missing keys and all keys that
20: do not start with `sk_test_`. Never run it with live-mode credentials. The Stripe
21: test account must have active membership prices under the lookup keys used by the
22: application. Every spec that creates customers, subscriptions, coupons, or
23: promotion codes owns cleanup from the first successful resource creation, except
24: durable account configuration explicitly shared with the application. The tier
25: signup spec creates missing `DHC_COACH_TIER` / `DHC_STUDENT_TIER` coupons and
26: retains them just like membership prices.
27: 
28: - `playwright.config.ts` starts the `e2e-phoenix-server` and `e2e-web-server` mise tasks; their task-local `env` tables define the test server environment.
29: - `playwright.config.ts` keeps `serviceWorkers: "block"`. The ALE-270 shell-caching worker re-issues same-origin requests from the worker, which bypasses `page.route` mocks (e.g. the Discord acceptance mock) without changing app behavior — every mocked-navigation test fails with the app working fine. Do not remove the block; the PWA shell spec asserts on static output only by design.
30: - `mix e2e.server` starts the application through a custom Mix task, so E2E-only Stripe coupon overrides are read in `config/test.exs` when `E2E_SERVER=true`; do not rely on production-only runtime configuration for the test server.
31: - `playwright.config.ts` appends its process ID to the configured `E2E_COMPOSE_PROJECT` prefix. Phoenix and global teardown inherit that value, giving every run an isolated Compose project instead of attaching to a stale database from another worktree.
32: - `mix e2e.server` starts the root Compose `test-db` through testcontainers-elixir, reads its dynamic port, migrates it, and starts Phoenix on `127.0.0.1:4000`.
33: - Keep the E2E Oban configuration at `plugins: []`, not `plugins: false`. Oban 2.23 uses peer leadership to stage scheduled jobs; `false` disables leadership even when queues are enabled and leaves delayed recovery jobs unexecuted.
34: - Global setup calls `POST /api/e2e/reset`, truncating application tables and restoring base settings.
35: - The suite currently uses one Playwright worker because legacy specs share run-level state. Add worker-partitioned databases before raising `workers`.
36: - HTML output is written to `apps/web/playwright-report`; machine-readable output is `apps/web/test-results/playwright-results.json`.
37: 
38: Docker and the Playwright Chromium/Firefox binaries are required. Install browsers with `pnpm --filter @dhc/web exec playwright install chromium firefox`.
39: 
40: On a macOS Docker VM (Colima, OrbStack, Lima, or Docker Desktop) the testcontainers harness needs the socket named on both sides, because the client and the container see different filesystems: `DOCKER_HOST` must be the client-side socket (e.g. `unix://$HOME/.colima/default/docker.sock`, since `DOCKER_HOST` is unset and `/var/run/docker.sock` is only a dangling symlink to Docker Desktop), and `TESTCONTAINERS_DOCKER_SOCKET_OVERRIDE=/var/run/docker.sock` must be the VM-side path that `mix e2e.server` bind-mounts into the Postgres container. Without them the harness fails before any test runs, with `{:docker_socket_not_found, ...}` and then `error while creating mount source path ... operation not supported`.
41: 
42: ## Phoenix test harness
43: 
44: The `/api/e2e/*` routes exist only when Phoenix compiles with `E2E_SERVER=true` under `MIX_ENV=test`. Every request requires the `x-e2e-harness-key` header. Never expose these routes in dev or production.
45: 
46: Use helpers from `setupFunctions.ts` for named domain fixtures:
47: 
48: - `createMember()`
49: - `setupWaitlistedUser()`
50: - `setupInvitedUser()`
51: - `createWorkshop()`
52: 
53: Membership pause/resume tests need an immediately active Stripe subscription:
54: pass `createSubscription: true` and `subscriptionPaymentMethod: "card"` to

Never assert CSS classes, computed styles (`toHaveCSS`), `data-*` attributes, element geometry (`boundingBox`), or DOM structure, and do not add production markup that only exists to be read by a spec (the one exception is the `data-app-hydrated` signal behind `gotoHydrated`, a wait rather than an assertion). `getByTestId` is acceptable as a locator of last resort, never as the thing asserted.
88: - When a visual or layout property is the contract (a full-screen mobile sheet, touch-target size), use `toHaveScreenshot` on content that is static across runs: set an explicit `page.setViewportSize`, and screenshot an element or page whose text does not include run-tagged fixture names or shared-run data. Baselines live in `e2e/<spec>-snapshots/` (darwin; E2E is not run in CI); create missing ones with `mise run test-e2e -- e2e/<spec>.spec.ts --update-snapshots=missing` (that pass reports each newly written baseline as a failure), rerun without the flag to confirm they match, and review the PNGs before committing. `e2e/screenshot.css` (wired as `expect.toHaveScreenshot.stylePath`) hides the TanStack Query Devtools button that the `pnpm dev` E2E server renders bottom-right; add any other dev-only overlay there rather than masking per test.
89: - Address the Stripe Payment Element through `e2e/stripe-payment.ts` (the iframe's accessible title, not Stripe's private wrapper class). Payment-step readiness is `signupSubmitButton(page)` becoming enabled; there is no hidden state element.

1: # Workshop venue autocomplete and directions
2: 
3: Status: scope summary confirmed by the user on 6 November 2026. No implementation,
4: Google provisioning or production changes authorized.
5: 
6: ALE-439 documentary validation is recorded in
7: [Google Places terms validation](google-places-terms-validation.md). Its provider
8: requirements must be resolved within the confirmed venue-name search scope;
9: address-only autofill was rejected as a replacement. Manual destinations remain
10: available independently. The native Calendar goal below is unchanged.
11: 
12: ## Goal
13: 
14: Help attendees navigate to the right venue from their Calendar Invitation and
15: attendee-facing workshop page. Google autocomplete is an aid to selecting that
16: destination, not a requirement for scheduling a workshop.
17: 
18: Calendar integration is already implemented. This feature extends it rather
19: than introducing another Calendar delivery path. See
20: [the integration guide](workshop-calendar.md).
21: 
22: ## Agreed decisions
23: 
24: Confirmed on 6 November 2026:
25: 
26: - Keep ordinary Google Maps venue-name search: search for a venue, deliberately
27:   select a result, save the destination, and use it for directions and Calendar's
28:   native location. The user explicitly rejected an address-only downgrade and
29:   further product-scope questions about that choice. Resolve provider details
30:   within this scope rather than presenting speculative restrictions as a reason
31:   to redesign it.
32: - Cover regular Workshop create/edit and Beginners' Workshop schedule/reschedule.
33: - Keep the existing short venue label separate from the selected Google location.
34:   Beginners' Workshop labels retain their existing 80-character email limit.
35: - Let staff enter a venue/address manually if Google has no suitable result or is
36:   unavailable, with an optional manually supplied Maps link.
37: - Favour Dublin in suggestions without excluding other locations.
38: - Show directions in Calendar events and attendee-facing workshop pages.
39: - Use Calendar's native location field, not a Maps link added to the event
40:   description. The goal is a recognizable, navigable venue in the Calendar UI.
41: - Include backfill for existing upcoming workshops, including those outside the
42:   normal regular Workshop edit window. Use a one-off reviewed mapping from
43:   existing venue text to selected destinations, with a preview of every affected
44:   upcoming workshop. Never silently choose the first Google search result; leave
45:   ambiguous venues unchanged for review. Past workshops stay untouched.
46: - Backfill follows the normal Calendar attendee-update mechanism, accepting that
47:   Google may send update emails. Enriching the same venue's destination details
48:   does not trigger separate workshop-rescheduled emails or change its date/time.
49:   It does not authorize moving a published workshop to another physical venue.
50:   No production backfill has been authorized or run.
51: - Leave existing email templates unchanged. This does not suppress Calendar's
52:   existing attendee-update notifications.
53: - Do not add an embedded map, coordinates requirement or shared venue directory.
54: - Preserve the separation between Workshop and Beginners' Workshop storage and
55:   commands. Reuse the existing Calendar synchronization protocol.
56: 
57: ## Verified integration constraints
58: 
59: - `Dhc.WorkshopCalendar.Sync` currently puts the source projection's `location`
60:   into Google's event `location` field. Committee event descriptions contain the
61:   protected dashboard link; participant events export no description.
62: - Google's Calendar event `location` is free-form text, not a structured Place ID
63:   field. A name/address can populate it, but this alone does not guarantee that
64:   Calendar resolves the intended Google Place. The published Calendar discovery
65:   schema also exposes no ordinary-event structured Place field. Verify the native
66:   location/navigation experience on an authorized isolated calendar rather than
67:   promising exact Place identity based on an API write alone.
68: - Existing published-Workshop editing restrictions and Beginners' Workshop
69:   reschedule/email policies remain in force unless explicitly changed here.
70: - Google Places has attribution and storage restrictions, including EEA-specific
71:   terms. The persistence strategy must be checked against the applicable terms;
72:   do not assume all returned place details can be stored indefinitely.
73: - Places requires its own API/billing/key configuration; existing Calendar OAuth
74:   does not establish that Places is configured.
75: - The owner confirmed that the intended Google Maps billing account is based in
76:   Ireland/EEA. Use that account region for validation; the actual project and any
77:   account-specific agreement have not been inspected.
78: 
79: ## Authorization boundary
80: 
81: No interview policy questions remain open. The user confirmed the complete scope
82: summary. Design confirmation is not permission to implement the feature, provision
83: Google, activate production sending, or backfill production records.
84: 
85: ## Implementation and verification scope
86: 
87: - Reuse one autocomplete input across the ordinary Workshop form and the
88:   Beginners' Workshop schedule/reschedule forms, preserving remote-form bindings,
89:   keyboard access, field errors and manual fallback.
90: - Extend each domain's own storage, request/read contracts and Calendar projection
91:   without merging their commands or tables. Regenerate the typed API client.
92: - Add attendee-facing directions links without exporting private Intake links,
93:   tokens or roster details to Google.
94: - Use the existing Calendar protocol for destination updates, preserving event
95:   identities, attendees, RSVPs, retry/fencing behaviour and historical cutoffs.
96: - Provide a preview/apply backfill through authorized source-owned operations,
97:   re-checking current rows before applying reviewed mappings. Do not bypass
98:   domain command ownership with direct database updates.
99: - Test form submissions, manual/failure paths, both API contracts, projections,
100:   backfill preview/application, normal Calendar update notifications and the
101:   absence of separate workshop-rescheduled emails for venue enrichment.
102: - Run affected frontend build/typecheck/lint/unit/browser/E2E coverage, Phoenix
103:   precommit and API generation/idempotency checks during implementation. Automated
104:   tests substitute Google; isolated live-Calendar acceptance requires separate
105:   authorization and synthetic data.
106: 
107: Provisional effort: 3–5 developer days, excluding Google provisioning and human
108: venue review. Native Calendar navigation behaviour and the applicable Places
109: storage terms remain technical validation gates, not claims already verified by
110: the design interview.
111: 
112: ## Sources
113: 
114: - [Google Calendar Events resource](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/v3/reference/events#location)
115: - [Google Places policies](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/policies)
116: - [Calendar specification, ALE-429](https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-429/spec-workshop-calendar-and-calendar-invitations)
117: - [Current Calendar launch scope, ALE-437](https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-437/calendar-launch-preview-and-explicit-activation)

1: # Google venue selection: what ALE-439 established
2: 
3: Checked against Google's public documentation on 6 November 2026.
4: 
5: ## Confirmed scope and account region
6: 
7: The user reconfirmed ordinary Google Maps venue-name search: search, deliberately
8: select a result, save the destination, and use it for directions and native
9: Calendar location. Address-only autofill was rejected as a replacement. This
10: product choice is settled; provider validation must work within it rather than
11: reopening the same scope question. The intended billing account is Ireland/EEA.
12: See the authoritative [venue design](google-maps-venue-design.md).
13: 
14: These confirmations record scope and account region. They do not establish a
15: licensing exception or authorize implementation, Google provisioning or
16: production operations.
17: 
18: ## Short answer
19: 
20: The feature is technically supported: search for a venue, select it, show the
21: destination, and write its address into Calendar's native `location` field.
22: Calendar describes that field as "Geographic location of the event as free-form
23: text." There is no Calendar-specific prohibition identified here. [Calendar API][calendar]
24: 
25: There are two different data flows:
26: 
27: - **Street-address autofill:** Google expressly exempts a selected street address
28:   that the user could have entered accurately themselves, for that user's
29:   specific transaction. Keeping the existing staff-written venue label and
30:   using this address for the workshop describes a different, narrower flow.
31: - **Venue/business lookup plus Place Details:** the chosen integration returns
32:   Google business names and addresses. Those fields are not automatically
33:   covered by the street-address exception. Their durable use remains unvalidated.
34: 
35: Custom licensing has not been shown necessary. The address-only flow is
36: reference material, not a proposed replacement for the confirmed venue search.
37: 
38: This report does not establish that the feature is prohibited. It also does not
39: clear ALE-439 or unblock ALE-442: data retention/reuse for the agreed venue
40: lookup remains to be validated under the applicable EEA terms.
41: Manual destinations can proceed independently. The agreed
42: [venue design](google-maps-venue-design.md) is unchanged.
43: 
44: ## The specific terms question
45: 
46: Google's [Places policy][policies] distinguishes these cases:
47: 
48: - **Ordinary Places results:** the general terms restrict copying/saving business
49:   names and addresses and caching content without an express exception. Place
50:   IDs may be stored indefinitely. A 30-day coordinates exception does not permit
51:   a 30-day address/name cache. [General terms §3.2.3][terms], [SST A.3/B.14.3][sst]
52: - **Selected street address:** the policy says the address is not subject to
53:   Maps Content restrictions when the end user could have supplied it completely
54:   and accurately without Autocomplete, solely for that user's specific
55:   transaction. This excludes suggestion lists, other content, and POI/address
56:   lookups offered by other Maps services. Selecting any business result does not
57:   automatically make all its returned fields exempt.
58: 
59: Keep the distinction explicit: an address selected as form input may qualify;
60: a business name/address discovered through Place Details is not automatically
61: covered. Copying a provider result into a "manual" field does not establish
62: independent provenance.
63: 
64: Google also documents address/geocode autocomplete excluding businesses. That
65: is a narrower integration and is not the chosen product scope. The published
66: street-address exception does not explicitly discuss Calendar attendee copies;
67: it must not be presented as either a guarantee for venue lookup or a reason to
68: require the rejected address-only replacement.
69: [Address-entry guidance][address-entry]
70: 
71: Before implementing Google-derived persistence, establish the permitted
72: retention/reuse for the exact venue selection/resolution flow. Report a concrete
73: provider limitation if one is established; do not infer either approval or a
74: need for a negotiated licence from an unresolved interpretation.
75: 
76: ### Which account terms apply?
77: 
78: EEA applicability follows the **Google billing account's address**, not the
79: club's name, server region or search location. The owner confirmed the intended
80: billing account is Ireland/EEA. Its project and any negotiated/reseller agreement
81: have not been inspected; the billing-region question is settled.
82: [EEA terms][eea-terms], [FAQ][eea-faq]
83: 
84: For an EEA account, the current SST permit address lookup/autocompletion but
85: limit other non-ID/non-coordinate Places uses to listed categories, and restrict
86: use "With any Map", including some links. Provider-supplied source links and
87: ID-only map linking have documented exceptions. Assess these rules only for
88: content that remains Google Maps Content. [EEA SST B.15][eea-sst],
89: [permitted uses][eea-uses], [EEA integration guide][eea-guide]
90: 
91: Do not assume an old project avoids EEA terms: the pre-8-July-2025 exception
92: requires an unmodified integration. The FAQ lists new services, methods and
93: response fields as material changes. Calendar OAuth is not evidence of an
94: existing Places integration. The terms pages checked were dated 26 August 2026;
95: both SST pages, 28 October 2026. These public pages do not establish the club's
96: accepted agreement.
97: 
98: ## Destination data contract
99: 
100: These decisions concern data handling, not a new shared venue database. Each
101: Workshop domain keeps its own storage and commands.
102: 
103: - **Staff-owned short label:** preserve it separately; do not populate it
104:   automatically from Google's business name. Keep the Beginners' Workshop
105:   80-character limit and existing email copy.
106: - **Independently supplied manual name/address/link:** can be saved, displayed
107:   to attendees and projected to Calendar without a Places dependency. The Maps
108:   link is optional and must pass server-side HTTPS/host/path/credential checks.
109:   Omission preserves the destination; explicit clear removes it; a manual
110:   replacement removes unrelated provider identity and derived links.
111: - **Suggestion text:** display only for the current search with attribution;
112:   discard when replaced, abandoned or unmounted. No database, persistent draft,
113:   CDN/service-worker cache, analytics or raw-response fixtures.
114: - **Selected name/address:** show a transient preview with attribution. Durable
115:   storage and attendee/Calendar reuse remain unresolved for non-exempt provider
116:   text. An address that actually meets the selected-address exception is treated
117:   according to that exception, not automatically as permanently restricted
118:   Places data. Do not invent a refresh TTL as a substitute for permission.
119: - **Place ID and provenance:** an ID may be stored indefinitely with
120:   `provider: google` and an application-generated selection/check timestamp.
121:   Google recommends refreshing IDs older than 12 months using Details `id`
122:   only. Clear on destination replacement/removal; obsolete or moved results
123:   require review, never automatic relocation of a workshop. [Place IDs][ids]
124: - **Directions URL:** construct a Maps URL from permitted destination text,
125:   optionally with the selected Place ID. Use `api=1`, `destination`, and optional
126:   `destination_place_id`; omit origin and encode values. No key is needed.
127:   Constructing a URL does not exempt restricted text inside it. Do not request
128:   or retain `googleMapsUri` merely to make a directions link. [Maps URLs][urls]
129: - **Attribution:** retain required credits alongside any retained non-exempt
130:   provider data under the permission that allows its retention. Raw responses,
131:   coordinates, photos, reviews and contact details are not part of the contract.
132: 
133: Calendar receives permitted name/address text, falling back to the existing
134: label. It has no ordinary structured Place-ID field; a successful text write
135: does not prove exact Place binding or native navigation quality. Exporting
136: non-exempt provider text, its retention in guest copies, and attribution remain
137: part of the unresolved assessment. Do not add description links as a workaround
138: or rewrite past events. Isolated native-navigation acceptance stays in ALE-445.
139: 
140: ## Lookup implementation contract
141: 
142: The technically supported candidate is **Autocomplete (New), then Place Details
143: (New) on deliberate selection**, through one domain-neutral Phoenix Req/Req.Test
144: boundary. It does not write workshops. The retention decision above must be
145: resolved before treating its preview fields as saved destination fields.
146: 
147: 1. Suggest: `POST https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places:autocomplete` with
148:    server-only `X-Goog-Api-Key`. Send `input`, random session token,
149:    `languageCode: en`, `regionCode: ie`, and `locationBias.circle` centred at
150:    `53.3498, -6.2603` with radius `30000` metres. Omit geographic restrictions,
151:    type filters, origin and query predictions. The circle biases toward Dublin
152:    without excluding other locations. Mask:
153:    `suggestions.placePrediction.placeId,suggestions.placePrediction.text.text`.
154:    Return ordered `{placeId, text}` suggestions; none is an empty success.
155:    [Autocomplete][autocomplete]
156: 2. Resolve: `GET https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places/{encodedPlaceId}` with
157:    the same session token, `languageCode=en` and mask
158:    `id,displayName,formattedAddress,attributions`. Map to a closed preview:
159:    `{provider: google, placeId, name, address, attributions}`. In New,
160:    `displayName.text` is the business name; `name` is a resource identifier.
161:    Map credits from `{provider, providerUri}`. Do not parse prediction text into
162:    authoritative name/address fields or expose raw JSON. [Details][details]
163: 3. Start a fresh UUID v4 per search interaction; end it on selection/resolution
164:    or abandonment. All calls in a session use the same Google project. Replacing
165:    a selection starts a new session. Debounce/cancel superseded searches and
166:    reject stale responses. Never use a workflow credential as the session token.
167:    [Sessions][sessions]
168: 4. Authenticate/capability-check and bound lookup requests. Return closed
169:    unavailable/configuration/quota/not-found failures, not provider bodies.
170:    Manual saving must work for every failure and when Places is unconfigured.
171:    Return lookup responses with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
172: 
173: Google receives only the venue query/ID, random session token, fixed bias and
174: language, field mask, key and normal server network metadata. Forward no browser
175: cookies, client-IP headers, Referer, workshop IDs/details or attendee facts.
176: Exclude lookup bodies/queries from logs, Sentry and analytics. Attendee links
177: must disclose only destination information and preserve no-referrer navigation,
178: especially on credential-bearing Intake pages.
179: 
180: ## Attribution and configuration
181: 
182: Display **Google Maps** branding in the suggestions container, selected-result
183: preview and any attendee surface displaying non-exempt Google data. Show returned
184: third-party credits too; keep them associated and visible on mobile. Manual
185: facts must not be falsely attributed to Google. Use the current official
186: logo/text/accessibility rules, and the application terms/privacy notices required
187: by the applicable agreement. A link or internal provider marker alone is not
188: attribution. [Places policy][policies]
189: 
190: Places needs its own billing-enabled project, **Places API (New)** enablement and
191: restricted server key. Restrict it to that API and the actual public egress IPs;
192: confirm stable egress before activation. No browser key is needed by this
193: candidate. A later Maps JavaScript choice needs a separate website-restricted
194: browser key and a fresh integration decision. Calendar organizer OAuth is

197: 
198: Review current quotas and session pricing before activation: requesting

200: standalone field-tier pricing. No zero-cost assumption is made.
201: [Session pricing][pricing]
202:

1: # Workshop venue autocomplete and directions
2: 
3: Status: scope summary confirmed by the user on 6 November 2026. No implementation,
4: Google provisioning or production changes authorized.
5: 
6: ALE-439 documentary validation is recorded in
7: [Google Places terms validation](google-places-terms-validation.md). Its provider
8: requirements must be resolved within the confirmed venue-name search scope;
9: address-only autofill was rejected as a replacement. Manual destinations remain
10: available independently. The native Calendar goal below is unchanged.
11: 
12: ## Goal
13: 
14: Help attendees navigate to the right venue from their Calendar Invitation and
15: attendee-facing workshop page. Google autocomplete is an aid to selecting that
16: destination, not a requirement for scheduling a workshop.
17: 
18: Calendar integration is already implemented. This feature extends it rather
19: than introducing another Calendar delivery path. See
20: [the integration guide](workshop-calendar.md).
21: 
22: ## Agreed decisions
23: 
24: Confirmed on 6 November 2026:
25: 
26: - Keep ordinary Google Maps venue-name search: search for a venue, deliberately
27:   select a result, save the destination, and use it for directions and Calendar's
28:   native location. The user explicitly rejected an address-only downgrade and
29:   further product-scope questions about that choice. Resolve provider details
30:   within this scope rather than presenting speculative restrictions as a reason
31:   to redesign it.
32: - Cover regular Workshop create/edit and Beginners' Workshop schedule/reschedule.
33: - Keep the existing short venue label separate from the selected Google location.
34:   Beginners' Workshop labels retain their existing 80-character email limit.
35: - Let staff enter a venue/address manually if Google has no suitable result or is
36:   unavailable, with an optional manually supplied Maps link.
37: - Favour Dublin in suggestions without excluding other locations.
38: - Show directions in Calendar events and attendee-facing workshop pages.
39: - Use Calendar's native location field, not a Maps link added to the event
40:   description. The goal is a recognizable, navigable venue in the Calendar UI.
41: - Include backfill for existing upcoming workshops, including those outside the
42:   normal regular Workshop edit window. Use a one-off reviewed mapping from
43:   existing venue text to selected destinations, with a preview of every affected
44:   upcoming workshop. Never silently choose the first Google search result; leave
45:   ambiguous venues unchanged for review. Past workshops stay untouched.
46: - Backfill follows the normal Calendar attendee-update mechanism, accepting that
47:   Google may send update emails. Enriching the same venue's destination details
48:   does not trigger separate workshop-rescheduled emails or change its date/time.
49:   It does not authorize moving a published workshop to another physical venue.
50:   No production backfill has been authorized or run.
51: - Leave existing email templates unchanged. This does not suppress Calendar's
52:   existing attendee-update notifications.
53: - Do not add an embedded map, coordinates requirement or shared venue directory.
54: - Preserve the separation between Workshop and Beginners' Workshop storage and
55:   commands. Reuse the existing Calendar synchronization protocol.
56: 
57: ## Verified integration constraints
58: 
59: - `Dhc.WorkshopCalendar.Sync` currently puts the source projection's `location`
60:   into Google's event `location` field. Committee event descriptions contain the
61:   protected dashboard link; participant events export no description.
62: - Google's Calendar event `location` is free-form text, not a structured Place ID
63:   field. A name/address can populate it, but this alone does not guarantee that
64:   Calendar resolves the intended Google Place. The published Calendar discovery
65:   schema also exposes no ordinary-event structured Place field. Verify the native
66:   location/navigation experience on an authorized isolated calendar rather than
67:   promising exact Place identity based on an API write alone.
68: - Existing published-Workshop editing restrictions and Beginners' Workshop
69:   reschedule/email policies remain in force unless explicitly changed here.
70: - Google Places has attribution and storage restrictions, including EEA-specific
71:   terms. The persistence strategy must be checked against the applicable terms;
72:   do not assume all returned place details can be stored indefinitely.
73: - Places requires its own API/billing/key configuration; existing Calendar OAuth
74:   does not establish that Places is configured.
75: - The owner confirmed that the intended Google Maps billing account is based in
76:   Ireland/EEA. Use that account region for validation; the actual project and any
77:   account-specific agreement have not been inspected.
78: 
79: ## Authorization boundary
80: 
81: No interview policy questions remain open. The user confirmed the complete scope
82: summary. Design confirmation is not permission to implement the feature, provision
83: Google, activate production sending, or backfill production records.
84: 
85: ## Implementation and verification scope
86: 
87: - Reuse one autocomplete input across the ordinary Workshop form and the
88:   Beginners' Workshop schedule/reschedule forms, preserving remote-form bindings,
89:   keyboard access, field errors and manual fallback.
90: - Extend each domain's own storage, request/read contracts and Calendar projection
91:   without merging their commands or tables. Regenerate the typed API client.
92: - Add attendee-facing directions links without exporting private Intake links,
93:   tokens or roster details to Google.
94: - Use the existing Calendar protocol for destination updates, preserving event
95:   identities, attendees, RSVPs, retry/fencing behaviour and historical cutoffs.
96: - Provide a preview/apply backfill through authorized source-owned operations,
97:   re-checking current rows before applying reviewed mappings. Do not bypass
98:   domain command ownership with direct database updates.
99: - Test form submissions, manual/failure paths, both API contracts, projections,
100:   backfill preview/application, normal Calendar update notifications and the
101:   absence of separate workshop-rescheduled emails for venue enrichment.
102: - Run affected frontend build/typecheck/lint/unit/browser/E2E coverage, Phoenix
103:   precommit and API generation/idempotency checks during implementation. Automated
104:   tests substitute Google; isolated live-Calendar acceptance requires separate
105:   authorization and synthetic data.
106: 
107: Provisional effort: 3–5 developer days, excluding Google provisioning and human
108: venue review. Native Calendar navigation behaviour and the applicable Places
109: storage terms remain technical validation gates, not claims already verified by
110: the design interview.
111:

1: # Google venue selection: what ALE-439 established
2: 
3: Checked against Google's public documentation on 6 November 2026.
4: 
5: ## Confirmed scope and account region
6: 
7: The user reconfirmed ordinary Google Maps venue-name search: search, deliberately
8: select a result, save the destination, and use it for directions and native
9: Calendar location. Address-only autofill was rejected as a replacement. This
10: product choice is settled; provider validation must work within it rather than
11: reopening the same scope question. The intended billing account is Ireland/EEA.
12: See the authoritative [venue design](google-maps-venue-design.md).
13: 
14: These confirmations record scope and account region. They do not establish a
15: licensing exception or authorize implementation, Google provisioning or
16: production operations.
17: 
18: ## Short answer
19: 
20: The feature is technically supported: search for a venue, select it, show the
21: destination, and write its address into Calendar's native `location` field.
22: Calendar describes that field as "Geographic location of the event as free-form
23: text." There is no Calendar-specific prohibition identified here. [Calendar API][calendar]
24: 
25: There are two different data flows:
26: 
27: - **Street-address autofill:** Google expressly exempts a selected street address
28:   that the user could have entered accurately themselves, for that user's
29:   specific transaction. Keeping the existing staff-written venue label and
30:   using this address for the workshop describes a different, narrower flow.
31: - **Venue/business lookup plus Place Details:** the chosen integration returns
32:   Google business names and addresses. Those fields are not automatically
33:   covered by the street-address exception. Their durable use remains unvalidated.
34: 
35: Custom licensing has not been shown necessary. The address-only flow is
36: reference material, not a proposed replacement for the confirmed venue search.
37: 
38: This report does not establish that the feature is prohibited. It also does not
39: clear ALE-439 or unblock ALE-442: data retention/reuse for the agreed venue
40: lookup remains to be validated under the applicable EEA terms.
41: Manual destinations can proceed independently. The agreed
42: [venue design](google-maps-venue-design.md) is unchanged.
43: 
44: ## The specific terms question
45: 
46: Google's [Places policy][policies] distinguishes these cases:
47: 
48: - **Ordinary Places results:** the general terms restrict copying/saving business
49:   names and addresses and caching content without an express exception. Place
50:   IDs may be stored indefinitely. A 30-day coordinates exception does not permit
51:   a 30-day address/name cache. [General terms §3.2.3][terms], [SST A.3/B.14.3][sst]
52: - **Selected street address:** the policy says the address is not subject to
53:   Maps Content restrictions when the end user could have supplied it completely
54:   and accurately without Autocomplete, solely for that user's specific
55:   transaction. This excludes suggestion lists, other content, and POI/address
56:   lookups offered by other Maps services. Selecting any business result does not
57:   automatically make all its returned fields exempt.
58: 
59: Keep the distinction explicit: an address selected as form input may qualify;
60: a business name/address discovered through Place Details is not automatically
61: covered. Copying a provider result into a "manual" field does not establish
62: independent provenance.
63: 
64: Google also documents address/geocode autocomplete excluding businesses. That
65: is a narrower integration and is not the chosen product scope. The published
66: street-address exception does not explicitly discuss Calendar attendee copies;
67: it must not be presented as either a guarantee for venue lookup or a reason to
68: require the rejected address-only replacement.
69: [Address-entry guidance][address-entry]
70: 
71: Before implementing Google-derived persistence, establish the permitted
72: retention/reuse for the exact venue selection/resolution flow. Report a concrete
73: provider limitation if one is established; do not infer either approval or a
74: need for a negotiated licence from an unresolved interpretation.
75: 
76: ### Which account terms apply?
77: 
78: EEA applicability follows the **Google billing account's address**, not the
79: club's name, server region or search location. The owner confirmed the intended
80: billing account is Ireland/EEA. Its project and any negotiated/reseller agreement
81: have not been inspected; the billing-region question is settled.
82: [EEA terms][eea-terms], [FAQ][eea-faq]
83: 
84: For an EEA account, the current SST permit address lookup/autocompletion but
85: limit other non-ID/non-coordinate Places uses to listed categories, and restrict
86: use "With any Map", including some links. Provider-supplied source links and
87: ID-only map linking have documented exceptions. Assess these rules only for
88: content that remains Google Maps Content. [EEA SST B.15][eea-sst],
89: [permitted uses][eea-uses], [EEA integration guide][eea-guide]
90: 
91: Do not assume an old project avoids EEA terms: the pre-8-July-2025 exception
92: requires an unmodified integration. The FAQ lists new services, methods and
93: response fields as material changes. Calendar OAuth is not evidence of an
94: existing Places integration. The terms pages checked were dated 26 August 2026;
95: both SST pages, 28 October 2026. These public pages do not establish the club's
96: accepted agreement.
97: 
98: ## Destination data contract
99: 
100: These decisions concern data handling, not a new shared venue database. Each
101: Workshop domain keeps its own storage and commands.
102: 
103: - **Staff-owned short label:** preserve it separately; do not populate it
104:   automatically from Google's business name. Keep the Beginners' Workshop
105:   80-character limit and existing email copy.
106: - **Independently supplied manual name/address/link:** can be saved, displayed
107:   to attendees and projected to Calendar without a Places dependency. The Maps
108:   link is optional and must pass server-side HTTPS/host/path/credential checks.
109:   Omission preserves the destination; explicit clear removes it; a manual
110:   replacement removes unrelated provider identity and derived links.
111: - **Suggestion text:** display only for the current search with attribution;
112:   discard when replaced, abandoned or unmounted. No database, persistent draft,
113:   CDN/service-worker cache, analytics or raw-response fixtures.
114: - **Selected name/address:** show a transient preview with attribution. Durable
115:   storage and attendee/Calendar reuse remain unresolved for non-exempt provider
116:   text. An address that actually meets the selected-address exception is treated
117:   according to that exception, not automatically as permanently restricted
118:   Places data. Do not invent a refresh TTL as a substitute for permission.
119: - **Place ID and provenance:** an ID may be stored indefinitely with
120:   `provider: google` and an application-generated selection/check timestamp.
121:   Google recommends refreshing IDs older than 12 months using Details `id`
122:   only. Clear on destination replacement/removal; obsolete or moved results
123:   require review, never automatic relocation of a workshop. [Place IDs][ids]
124: - **Directions URL:** construct a Maps URL from permitted destination text,
125:   optionally with the selected Place ID. Use `api=1`, `destination`, and optional
126:   `destination_place_id`; omit origin and encode values. No key is needed.
127:   Constructing a URL does not exempt restricted text inside it. Do not request
128:   or retain `googleMapsUri` merely to make a directions link. [Maps URLs][urls]
129: - **Attribution:** retain required credits alongside any retained non-exempt
130:   provider data under the permission that allows its retention. Raw responses,
131:   coordinates, photos, reviews and contact details are not part of the contract.
132: 
133: Calendar receives permitted name/address text, falling back to the existing
134: label. It has no ordinary structured Place-ID field; a successful text write
135: does not prove exact Place binding or native navigation quality. Exporting
136: non-exempt provider text, its retention in guest copies, and attribution remain
137: part of the unresolved assessment. Do not add description links as a workaround
138: or rewrite past events. Isolated native-navigation acceptance stays in ALE-445.
139: 
140: ## Lookup implementation contract
141: 
142: The technically supported candidate is **Autocomplete (New), then Place Details
143: (New) on deliberate selection**, through one domain-neutral Phoenix Req/Req.Test
144: boundary. It does not write workshops. The retention decision above must be
145: resolved before treating its preview fields as saved destination fields.
146: 
147: 1. Suggest: `POST https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places:autocomplete` with
148:    server-only `X-Goog-Api-Key`. Send `input`, random session token,
149:    `languageCode: en`, `regionCode: ie`, and `locationBias.circle` centred at
150:    `53.3498, -6.2603` with radius `30000` metres. Omit geographic restrictions,
151:    type filters, origin and query predictions. The circle biases toward Dublin
152:    without excluding other locations. Mask:
153:    `suggestions.placePrediction.placeId,suggestions.placePrediction.text.text`.
154:    Return ordered `{placeId, text}` suggestions; none is an empty success.
155:    [Autocomplete][autocomplete]
156: 2. Resolve: `GET https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places/{encodedPlaceId}` with
157:    the same session token, `languageCode=en` and mask
158:    `id,displayName,formattedAddress,attributions`. Map to a closed preview:
159:    `{provider: google, placeId, name, address, attributions}`. In New,
160:    `displayName.text` is the business name; `name` is a resource identifier.
161:    Map credits from `{provider, providerUri}`. Do not parse prediction text into
162:    authoritative name/address fields or expose raw JSON. [Details][details]
163: 3. Start a fresh UUID v4 per search interaction; end it on selection/resolution
164:    or abandonment. All calls in a session use the same Google project. Replacing
165:    a selection starts a new session. Debounce/cancel superseded searches and
166:    reject stale responses. Never use a workflow credential as the session token.
167:    [Sessions][sessions]
168: 4. Authenticate/capability-check and bound lookup requests. Return closed
169:    unavailable/configuration/quota/not-found failures, not provider bodies.
170:    Manual saving must work for every failure and when Places is unconfigured.
171:    Return lookup responses with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
172: 
173: Google receives only the venue query/ID, random session token, fixed bias and
174: language, field mask, key and normal server network metadata. Forward no browser
175: cookies, client-IP headers, Referer, workshop IDs/details or attendee facts.
176: Exclude lookup bodies/queries from logs, Sentry and analytics. Attendee links
177: must disclose only destination information and preserve no-referrer navigation,
178: especially on credential-bearing Intake pages.
179: 
180: ## Attribution and configuration
181: 
182: Display **Google Maps** branding in the suggestions container, selected-result
183: preview and any attendee surface displaying non-exempt Google data. Show returned
184: third-party credits too; keep them associated and visible on mobile. Manual
185: facts must not be falsely attributed to Google. Use the current official
186: logo/text/accessibility rules, and the application terms/privacy notices required
187: by the applicable agreement. A link or internal provider marker alone is not
188: attribution. [Places policy][policies]
189: 
190: Places needs its own billing-enabled project, **Places API (New)** enablement and
191: restricted server key. Restrict it to that API and the actual public egress IPs;
192: confirm stable egress before activation. No browser key is needed by this
193: candidate. A later Maps JavaScript choice needs a separate website-restricted
194: browser key and a fresh integration decision. Calendar organizer OAuth is
195: separate. No setup or billing/key changes were performed. [Setup][setup],
196: [key security][security]
197: 
198: Review current quotas and session pricing before activation: requesting
199: `displayName` is not an ID-only lookup, and session billing differs from
200: standalone field-tier pricing. No zero-cost assumption is made.
201: [Session pricing][pricing]
202: 
203: ## Checks for the later autocomplete ticket
204: 
205: - Substitute Google with synthetic Req.Test data. Assert the exact calls/masks,
206:   session lifecycle, non-exclusive Dublin bias, closed mapping, empty results,
207:   quota/auth/outage handling and stale-response rejection.
208: - Test real form submissions through all four workflows, manual fallback,
209:   replacement/clear/omission, field errors, keyboard/phone behaviour and the
210:   short-label limit. Test the resolved field permission/retention rules, not an
211:   assumed blanket right to save provider JSON.
212: - Check attribution and privacy on selected results and every attendee surface;
213:   verify no persistent lookup cache or credential-bearing requests/referrers.
214: - Run the existing substituted Calendar protocol against real source changes:
215:   native location, preserved event/RSVP identity, normal updates, no-op silence
216:   and enrichment without false reschedule emails. Live acceptance and production
217:   operations still require separate authorization.

     4

     6	  attendee: a recognizable name and address for the same place, plus an
     7	  optional manually supplied Google Maps link used for directions. The label
     8	  stays required and independent in every source context; a destination never
     9	  replaces it.
    10	
    11	  This module owns the two rules every workshop-owning context shares:
    12	
    13	    * which manually supplied URLs are supported HTTPS Maps destinations, and
    14	    * how a destination composes the recognizable Calendar location string,
    15	      falling back to the source's own label when no destination is stored.
    16	
    17	  It is deliberately free of workshop policy: storage, commands and scheduling
    18	  stay with each source context (ADR 0029), and no provider response shape or
    19	  provider identity lives here — a Google-selected destination (later work)
    20	  will reuse these seams without either context importing the other.
    21	
    22	  ## URL scope
    23	
    24	  Only `https` links on Google's Maps surfaces are accepted: executable and
    25	  non-secure schemes, embedded credentials, explicit ports, and hosts or paths
    26	  outside Maps are refused. The check is a safety allowlist, not an attempt to
    27	  prove the link resolves to a particular place; a name/address remains useful
    28	  without a link, and a link without a provider listing is a valid destination.

    32	  @address_max 500
    33	  @url_max 2048

    38	  @google_hosts ~w(maps.google.com)

   103

   105	  The one user-facing sentence for each `validate_maps_url/1` refusal.

   155	
   156	  defp check_scheme(%URI{scheme: scheme}) do
   157	    if scheme != nil and String.downcase(scheme) == "https",

   160	  end

   169	
   170	  defp check_target(%URI{host: host, path: path}) when is_binary(host) do

   177	      host in @short_link_maps_path_hosts -> maps_path?(path)
   178	      true -> {:error, :unsupported_target}
   179	    end
   180	  end
   181	
   182	  defp check_target(_uri), do: {:error, :invalid_url}
   183

   185	    if String.starts_with?(path || "/", "/maps"),
   186	      do: :ok,
   187	      else: {:error, :unsupported_target}
   188	  end
   189	end

**Manual step after `mise run api-gen`**: `packages/api-client/src/index.ts` is hand-maintained (tracked, not generated). `openapi-ts` only writes to `src/client/`; it does not update the public re-exports in `src/index.ts`. After adding a new operation, manually add the generated SDK function plus its `types.gen` / `valibot.gen` / `@tanstack/svelte-query.gen` exports to the four `export` blocks in `src/index.ts` (mirror how `waitlistStatus` / `membersInsuranceForm` are exposed). Without this, the function exists in `src/client/` but is not importable from `@dhc/api-client`.

`packages/api-client/openapi-ts.config.ts` explicitly points `output.tsConfigPath` at `packages/api-client/tsconfig.json` so postinstall generation works in deployment environments that do not expose the repo-root SvelteKit `tsconfig.json`.

## Findings

1. **E2E cleanup violation** — `apps/web/e2e/workshop-management.spec.ts:1110-1125` creates real Stripe Checkout-session cleanup, but calls `expireSessions()` only after browser assertions. Any failure at lines 1112–1123 skips cleanup and leaks the real test-mode session. `apps/web/e2e/AGENTS.md:19-26,74` requires Stripe resources be cleaned up and forbids assertions from preventing cleanup. Put the assertions in `try` and call `expireSessions()` in `finally`.

No other documented-standard violations or sufficiently concrete Fowler smells found in the uncommitted `but diff` (including added files).
